options: Right: private firms move up along their own demand as the rate rises, so they borrow less; the government's borrowing makes up more than the increase in the total.

why.correct: Crowding out has a long-run cost: a smaller capital stock and slower growth of potential output.

why.correct: Crowding out depends on how far the real interest rate rises; more saving limits the rise.

why.correct: Higher real interest rate, lower private investment, slower growth of the capital stock.

The real rate rises, not falls.

options: In a deep recession private demand for funds is weak, so government borrowing raises the real rate less.

why.correct: Economic growth: the PPC shifts out and LRAS shifts right, so real GDP per capita can rise year after year.
